subject: Telescoped prepay credit structure and true-up mechanism
messages:
From: Arielle Katz <arielle.katz@synerbyte.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Ethan Morris <ethan.m@synerbyte.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Telescoped prepay — can we model credits + true-up?

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. SynerByte is evaluating a multi-year prepay to lock pricing and simplify procurement (likely 2.5–3.0M ARR run rate over the next 12 months). Finance wanted to explore a telescoped credit approach rather than a flat % discount — essentially larger effective credit early in the term and a scheduled step-down, with an annual true-up to align consumption.

High-level asks:
- Can you show an example three-year structure with a telescoped credit (year 1 > year 2 > year 3) and an explicit true-up mechanism?
- We need suggested invoicing cadence (annual vs. quarterly) and any recommended split for partial upfront payments.
- Any limits or gating (minimum committed baseline) required to qualify for the full credit?

Ethan and I can share consumption forecasts if that helps. Ideally we’d have a concrete term-sheet for procurement to review this week.

Thanks,
Arielle
Arielle Katz
VP, Finance | SynerByte
aris.katz@synerbyte.com | +1 650-555-0142

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Arielle Katz <arielle.katz@synerbyte.com>
Cc: Ethan Morris <ethan.m@synerbyte.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telescoped prepay — can we model credits + true-up?

Hi Arielle / Ethan —

Great question — yes, we can do a telescoped prepay structure and a simple annual true-up. Attached is a short term-sheet and an Excel model with three scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive) so you can see how the effective unit price evolves if consumption deviates. Key points below: 

Proposal (illustrative):
- Term: 3 years (36 months) with an option to annualize at the end of year 2.
- Credit profile (example): Year 1 = 26% effective credit on listed rates; Year 2 = 18%; Year 3 = 12%. Credits are applied as an upfront prepayment credit allocation.
- Ramp & gating: A minimum committed baseline (50% of year 1 projected usage) must be prepaid to qualify for the year 1 credit. The remaining prepay can be staged across year boundaries per the Excel schedule.
- Invoicing: Prefer single annual invoice at the start of each contract year (improves accounting for both parties). We can support split invoicing (50/50 annually) if you need cash-flow smoothing.
- True-up: Annual true-up within 45 days of the contract year close. Consumption above the prepaid amount is invoiced at the net post-credit rate for that year; consumption below results in a one-time reconciliation credit applied to the next invoice. No clawback within the first 12 months if usage is within a 10% tolerance band.
- Early-exit / stepdown: If SynerByte terminates early, unused prepaid credit is refundable on a pro-rata basis minus a 5% administrative fee, unless termination is for cause.

Next steps: If this matches what procurement needs, I can request an internal discount approval for the Year 1 credit and circulate a final DocuSign term-sheet. I copied our pricing lead (Karthik) and finance approver (Kimberly) so we can accelerate.

I attached: RB-2026-SYB-079-proposed-term-sheet.pdf and telescoped-prepay-excel.xlsx (baseline scenario shown).

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Approval request — SynerByte telescoped prepay (RB-2026-SYB-079)

Karthik / Kimberly —

Looping you in for quick approval on the proposed telescoped credits for SynerByte (deal RB-2026-SYB-079). Customer wants a 3-year structure with the effective credit profile: Y1=26%, Y2=18%, Y3=12%. We are gating the full Y1 credit on a 50% prepaid baseline. Invoice annual (preferred by customer).

Revenue impact / ask:
- ARR uplift if they choose aggressive scenario: ~2.9M in prepaid in Y1.
- Margin / unit economics: shown in attached spreadsheet; net blended discount over 3 years ~18%.

Specific approvals requested:
1) Approve Year 1 credit at 26% (exception to standard max 20% for multi-year prepay).
2) Approve the 50% prepaid baseline gating to limit downside.
3) Confirm refund/clawback language (we suggested pro-rata refund minus 5% admin).

If you prefer, we can reduce Y1 to 24% and increase the tolerance band for true-up from 10% to 15% to lower exposure. Customer is sensitive to cash flow and prefers heavier early credit in exchange for upfront cash.

I need a sign-off today to meet procurement timing — they want the DocuSign link by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request — SynerByte telescoped prepay (RB-2026-SYB-079)

Jonas —

Approve with one adjustment. I will sign off on the 26% Y1 / 18% Y2 / 12% Y3 profile provided we: 
- Change the true-up tolerance from 10% to 12.5% (gives a slightly wider buffer for forecast variance).
- Require split invoicing option (annual or 50/50 at start/mid-year) to be selectable on the contract; default to annual but allow customer to elect split for year 1 only.

Keep the 50% prepaid baseline gating and the pro-rata refund minus 5% admin fee. Ask Jonas to send final term-sheet via DocuSign and include a clause that any usage above the prepaid amount in year 1 is charged at the year 1 post-credit rate (no retroactive increase).

Jonas — please send the DocuSign link and loop in Legal if SynerByte requests any redlines on termination.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 212-555-0033
